semantic_mapping_proof.fact: Graph construction creates carry input before optional prior input. Lag1 graph concatenates prior then carry; the actual role4 first region maps node0concat/node1concat/node3cast/node4binary and its inputport2 is the prior hidden. Role3 step5/node8cast is the same original carry hidden converted for MTP pre_fc_norm_hidden. The instance numbers are physical plan indices, not global stable logical IDs.

Layer0 history input is BF16[1,3,6144], exactly36,864B. Its concat with the new projected qkv is actual step63 input0; the observed36,864->73,728 shift moves from slot1 to slot2 of that real layer0 history pool.

After publishing the all-row hidden output, construction makes separate normalized-row0 and row1 Copies. The observed late output step is the first Copy, carry_ports[0][0], not the fixed Phase.hidden tensor or the draft score output.

allocation_and_acceptance_root_cause.fact: For N1/R1/two boundaries, each conv/GDN pool has3 physical state allocations; the hidden pool has4 rows. Each verify obtains new ordinary leases: next then first conv/GDN states, and carry row0 then row1. All these are real snapshot/candidate material, not scratch replicas of a current state.

LeasePool allocates a fresh generation from a shared bounded free-range allocator using bytes/alignment only. It has no role/Invocation/previous-capture-offset affinity. Released/coalesced free ranges and selected live versions determine which physical offset becomes available; equal schema or lease size is not an address-stability promise.

After actual completion and accepted1/2 selection, next snapshot takes first or next recurrent/conv boundary. Target row0 becomes carry on accepted1, or prior on accepted2 while row1 becomes carry. Only after all export/take/ready/unbind work does one head swap commit. Old head and in-flight candidate ownership preserve rollback and snapshot readers.

Consequently role/slot revisits can see a different correct prior/carry/conv allocation, or receive a different correct output candidate range even though native backing handle, dtype, shape and strides match. The actual10records are these offset changes. The round7 conv case follows the earlier rejection selecting the first boundary, then returning to the previously captured lag0 role/slot; it is not a changed attention schedule.

legality.conclusion: Correct mandatory invalidation for the current command representation. Recorded commands contain full physical argument addresses: same allocation handle plus another offset is a different address. stable=1 proves identity only when the complete TensorView tuple remains equal; it does not permit changing offsets. Treating these as content-only updates could launch stale pointers and cross snapshot boundaries.

safe_next_directions_without_shadow_payl.current_gap: LeasePool/RangeAllocator currently expose only bytes/alignment allocation, not an exact/preferred-free-range request. safe_next_directions_without_shadow_payl.safety: Never pin extra hidden/conv payload as a capture cache, retain rejected candidate storage beyond the real version budget, or overwrite old head merely because its ReadLease is unique. Current head must survive graph/selector failure; prefix/snapshot/native-use owners can keep a preferred range occupied. Count every real allocation and preserve N+2R / hidden2(N+R) budgets.

safe_next_directions_without_shadow_payl.direction: If the remaining semantic input-address rotations dominate, use an explicit backend-qualified command-argument update/indirection capability rather than weakening TensorView identity.

It is larger than an allocator affinity hint and is not implemented or justified by range counts alone.
safe_next_directions_without_shadow_payl.safety: Same backing handle is insufficient. The current backend/Graph contract does not promise arbitrary offset updates, and immutable old snapshots, shared prefixes, other sessions and failed candidates must remain isolated.

existing_mechanisms: LeasePool and RangeAllocator already bound backing and metadata. Free-bin selection, alignment, splitting and coalescing choose offsets; neither public allocator accepts a preferred address or offset.

ReadLease::try_write can reuse an existing block only when whole-block ownership is unique and native uses have retired. Snapshot aliases and real native uses keep the range alive. Allocation generation and actual retirement remain authoritative.

The consumer allocates candidate first/next recurrent, convolution and hidden boundaries from these pools; selection, unselected candidates and pinned snapshots naturally change the available range order. Model execution parity is not a physical state-slot assignment.
Graph preserves dormant recordings only subject to complete preparation and exact resource/handle/offset/extent/permission identity. A stable allocation handle alone is insufficient.
The CUDA backend currently captures a new graph and instantiates it; the current Hyle capture extension has no update operation. Existing status-word reuse does not update graph parameters.

consumer_address_affinity.possible_basis: A bounded, ownership-aware preference could retain and safely promote an actual retired block via existing try_write; any unavailable, failed or pinned block must fall back to normal allocation.
consumer_address_affinity.missing_piece: There is no address-hint allocator API or output-writer return API. Reusing state owners across every create/rebuild/selection/abort path would require additional consumer ownership bookkeeping and could add per-step work. Retained idle owners must still fit the existing physical backing and live-version bounds.
consumer_address_affinity.decision: Not adopted. No small, proved allocation-order change currently eliminates these losses across acceptance choices, prefix pins and multiple sessions. Do not restructure 36 state pools solely from the 10-event count.

generic_capture_update.vendor_basis: The locally installed CUDA 13.3 cuda_runtime_api.h:12820-12910 exposes cudaGraphExecUpdate for compatible freshly captured graphs, subject to topology, node, context and parameter restrictions.
generic_capture_update.current_gap: Hyle currently destroys the covering recording on physical-binding invalidation and exposes no update API. A correct future path must retain an idle old artifact as nonlaunchable, fully revalidate new bindings/owners, capture the new graph, check update status/result and fall back to fresh instantiate. Context, checked-status and true retirement ownership must remain valid throughout.
generic_capture_update.limit: This still performs new capture and preparation; it can only avoid the eligible instantiation portion. Opaque vendor node parameters must not be patched or assumed compatible.
generic_capture_update.decision: Not adopted in this batch. No current API can safely substitute this behavior without an explicit owner/lifecycle contract.

findings: The original P154/64 natural MTP workload completed once with64 actual IDs and selected work fields equal to the frozen AD run. Scratch logging records only metadata and emits after the original workload; tensor payload copies are suppressed.

Ten actual retained capture ranges were erased. All first observed causes were qualified ordinary tensor binding tuple changes with same resource/native allocation but different byte offset, not native-plan callback, unproven identity, Queue replacement or permission-release loss.

Nine first changed ports are MTP prior/carry hidden pool views; one is the layer0 conv history input. Read aliases and candidate output aliases vary with accepted-prefix state selection and ordinary pooled range reuse.

Physical argument changes require invalidation under the original captured-command contract. The same backing allocation is not proof that a different subrange may replay through old pointer arguments.
Each event captures only the first changed port which causes a whole retained range to be erased. It is not an exhaustive diff of every later port or proof all history/state movement was observed.
Existing Graph invalidation and state lifetime contracts remain unchanged. No public diagnostic API, new executor, shadow state copy, unsafe preservation or performance improvement is introduced.

All observed losses occur in decode rounds4..15, followed by complete recorded-range reuse. The7 affected calls have18.1936ms inclusive cold buckets in this instrumented process, not a measurement of invalidation self-time or recoverable performance. The next finite investigation is actual no-recapture MTP steady-state hotspots.

This batch closes the actual first-cause attribution gap for the current AD-shaped workload. Historical W data retains its original scope; matching total counts alone do not retroactively prove those old causes.
